items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: At Tom Anderson, they used two guitars... There were two men in the band. Snow and this other fella, Charlie Washington... Well, he was the leader. And then I played bass, you know.

ctx.x: No, he wasn't too loud, but he could play good though. Yeah. And... Well, then they used... At Tom Anderson, they used two guitars, you see. Because they had more vocal. The fellas... There were two men in the band. Snow and this other fella, Charlie Washington. Them two fellas could sing. And this other fella, Tom Brown, who played the mandolin. He could play mandolin by note. But he read music. Yeah. Well, he was the leader. And then I played bass, you know. I'd taken Sam Orange's place on the bass. And I…

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: I think it was Walter Preston, Tom Brown, uh, Charlie Washington... But anyway, sometimes I used to play bass with them, too.

ctx.x: Well, he, he played with that, it wasn't such a big band, it was just about three or four pieces, or five pieces, I think it was Walter Preston, Tom Brown, uh, Charlie Washington, and, uh, let's see, what's that guy named, uh, I can't think of the bass player. But anyway, sometimes I used to play bass with them, too. And they used to go out, they used to play out at the halfway house, though. They had a, a place on that side of the halfway house, you could go in and play music. And then from there they'd go out…
Was Charlie Washington any kind of Lonzo Washington?
